sentences.text: Atacamatitan was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that likely weighed between 8 and 16 tonnes. Scientists know this animal from a preserved right femur measuring 1.10 meters in length.
The gracile nature of this bone suggests the creature had stronger forelimbs than its hindlimbs.

Chilean and Brazilian researchers began preliminary fossil hunting expeditions in the Antofagasta Region of Chile in February 2000. The genus was formally named and described by Alexander et al. in 2011.
Atacamatitan belongs to the unranked superfamily Titanosauria. In its original description, it was classified within the family Titanosauridae.
A 2012 cladistic analysis by Rubilar-Rogers and Gutstein later placed the genus within the clade Lithostrotia.
Fossils of this animal were found in the Atacama Desert in northern Chile. It lived during the Cenomanian to Maastrichtian stages, between 100.5 and 66 million years ago.
Most cladistic analyses exclude Atacamatitan due to the fragmentary nature of the holotype — the specimen the species is based on.
